title: A Fine-Grained Semantic Segmentation Method for Industrial Heritage Built Environments: Local–Global Feature Enhancement and Class-Discriminative Constraints
content: The conservation of industrial heritage has shifted from mere physical preservation to adaptive reuse; accurately distinguishing between historical components, later modifications, and other architectural elements is crucial for quantitative spatial analysis and renovation assessment. However, maintaining historic character often makes elements with different semantic attributes visually similar. Key challenges include subtle local differences between similar classes, insufficient coordination between local details and global context, and class imbalance causing intra-class dispersion and inter-class overlap. Using the Tianjin First Machine Tool Fac-tory as a case study, this study constructs a 14-class foreground semantic dataset and proposes Enhanced Mask2Former for Heritage Gardens (Hg-Mask2Former++). Based on Mask2Former-Swin-B, the model introduces LGFE to enhance multi-scale local–global representations and CDCC to optimize class relationships through class-balanced sampling and supervised contrastive learning. With only a 1.49% parameter increase, Hg-Mask2Former++ achieves 73.92% mIoU and 82.67% mDice, improving the baseline by 2.12 and 1.86 percentage points. Under identical experimental settings, its mIoU exceeds that of eight comparison models, including FastVim, TPSegformer, and ViT-P-based models proposed in 2026; the IoU of Industrial Building and Modern Building improves by about 20 percentage points. Further experiments reveal class-selective and condi-tion-dependent gains, indicating that scene-specific targeted optimization is more suitable than simply increasing network complexity.
